actual_scope: Answer #3702 (odd-kernel-coeff-bit-tariff) OQ1: under three named alternate ADDRESS physical tariffs (max-height, shared-denominator packing, odd-core modulus-dependent), every certified odd kernel q in {3,5,7,9,15} fails to strictly beat the dyadic fused and baseline bills on j in 0..32 (0 beats; one max-height baseline tie at (q=3,j=0) with bill 22). Distinct from the published #3702 bit-sum tariff; max-height and packing are sign-sensitive so bills use signed power lists.
scope_change_reason: The drawn connector-alphabet card is redirected to the unanswered alternate-tariff obligation left open by #3702 after the bit-sum census; this is a scoped #840-style multi-tariff cost lemma on the same ADDRESS lowering, not a reprint of the bit-sum 165+165 grid.
bottleneck_link: A single named bit-sum tariff leaving open whether max-height / packing / modulus-dependent encodings reorder odd vs dyadic; closing that obligation prevents a false physical win from an unexamined alternate cost model.
stop_rule: Stop after naming the three alternate tariffs, proving distinctness from bit-sum, locking the 0-beat census (with the one baseline tie), independent replay and package controls. No BIT-supplier hosting search and no new kappa.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json, PROOF.md, tariff.py, verify.py, independent.py and test_package.py. On j=0..32 under each named alternate tariff, odd fused beats = 0 and odd baseline beats = 0; max-height baseline ties once at (3,0) with bill 22.
